parsed.stack: Web-first (students are on school laptops and phones), Next.js + Supabase. Notes anchored to the text the student already owns - the app never ships the copyrighted set text; anchoring is by quoted phrase plus paragraph index, not page number, so it survives different print editions. On-device model on phones where available, otherwise a small cloud text call with the class's accumulated notes cached at ~90% off. Class link join, no accounts for read-only. Freemium subscription.
milestones: Week 1-2: line-anchor engine - match a student's quoted phrase to a canonical position in the text without hosting the text, across editions.
Week 3-4: class-link join and the shared annotation layer, visible only to link holders, with moderation the teacher can ignore.
Week 5-6: rating and the pre-mock surfacing of the highest-rated line notes per chapter.
Week 7-8: shareable annotated-chapter artefact (the growth loop) and the freemium gate on second and third set texts.
Week 9: seed into six A-level and IB English classes through teachers, measure student-written notes per class.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That notes can be reliably anchored to specific lines of a copyrighted set text the app is not allowed to host, across the four or five print and ebook editions a single class will be holding - get this wrong and every shared note lands in the wrong place, which is the product.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Take one set text, collect the three commonest editions plus the ebook, and test phrase-to-position matching on 100 quoted lines in a script - a day's work and no product.
